name: Elioenai
overview: Elioenai is a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Neariah. His mention in Scripture is concise, focusing on his genealogy without additional narrative or personal details. There are no further notes expanding on his life or role beyond his lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Elioenai means 'my eyes [look] to YHWH,' reflecting a devotional orientation toward the LORD. This proper name, referenced in 1 Chronicles 3:23, does not appear to be given directly by God but carries a meaningful expression of faith embedded in its Hebrew form.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elioenai as the son of Neariah. Additionally, several other individuals—Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani—are inferred to be his ancestors, indicating a detailed genealogical line within Judah. No other familial connections are documented in the provided data.
scriptureSignificance: Elioenai's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical records of Judah, serving as a link in the lineage that traces the descendants of the tribe. His name's meaning underscores a spiritual focus on the LORD, which aligns with the broader biblical emphasis on faithfulness to God. While the biblical text does not detail his personal deeds, his inclusion in the genealogy affirms the continuity of God's covenantal promises through Judah's descendants.
